item.title: Government: "Japan's Fukushima Treated Water Discharge Resumes After Suspension... Momentary Power Outage Caused the Halt" (정부 “중단됐던 日 후쿠시마 오염수 방류 재개… 순간 정전이 중단 원인”)
item.description:
Government: "Japan's Fukushima Treated Water Discharge Resumes After Suspension... Momentary Power Outage Caused the Halt" (정부 “중단됐던 日 후쿠시마 오염수 방류 재개… 순간 정전이 중단 원인”)

The South Korean government announced that the discharge of treated radioactive water from Japan's Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant was temporarily suspended on the 13th due to equipment malfunction and has since resumed. The discharge had previously been halted on the 10th due to an alarm and resumed the following day. (일본 후쿠시마 제1원자력발전소 방사능 오염 처리수 방류가 13일 설비 이상으로 일시 중단됐다가 재개됐다고 한국 정부가 밝혔다. 방류는 지난 10일에도 경보로 중단됐다가 이튿날 재개된 바 있다.)

Kim Young-soo, First Deputy Director of the Office for Government Policy Coordination, stated in a written briefing at 9:13 p.m. on the same day, "Tokyo Electric Power Company (TEPCO) reported that the 20th discharge of treated water was automatically halted at around 5:04 p.m. today (the 13th) due to an alarm in the water transfer process, and the cause is currently under investigation." (김영수 국무조정실 국무1차장은 이날 오후 9시 13분 서면 브리핑을 통해 “도쿄전력은 20차 오염수 방류가 오늘(13일) 오후 5시 4분경 오염수 이송 공정 경보 발생으로 자동 중지됐으며, 현재 원인을 파악 중이라고 밝혔다”고 전했다.)

In a subsequent written briefing at 11:42 p.m. that day, Deputy Director Kim said, "The discharge resumed at around 10:34 p.m., and equipment inspection showed no abnormalities." (김 차장은 이후 이날 오후 11시 42분 서면 브리핑을 통해 “오후 10시 34분경 방류가 재개됐으며, 설비 점검 결과 설비에는 이상이 없는 것으로 나타났다”고 밝혔다.)

Regarding the reason for the automatic halt, Deputy Director Kim explained, "A momentary power outage caused a decrease in the flow rate of the seawater transfer pump, which triggered the emergency shutoff valve." (김 차장은 방류가 자동 중지됐던 이유에 대해 “순간 정전에 의해 해수 이송 펌프의 유량이 저하돼 긴급 차단 밸브가 작동했었기 때문”이라고 전했다.)

Since the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake and the subsequent accident at the Fukushima Daiichi plant, TEPCO has been storing treated radioactive water in tanks. The water, which has been processed through the Advanced Liquid Processing System (ALPS) to remove radioactive substances, has been accumulated in batches and released into the sea since 2023. (도쿄전력은 2011년 동일본 대지진의 여파로 후쿠시마 1원전에서 일어난 사고를 처리하는 과정에서 생긴 방사능 오염수를 수조에 보관해 왔고, ‘다핵종 제거 설비(ALPS)’를 통해 방사능 물질을 걸러내는 처리를 거친 물을 일정량씩 모아뒀다가 2023년부터 바다에 흘려보내고 있다.)

TEPCO began the 20th discharge on the 1st of this month, but it was automatically halted at 4:17 p.m. on the 10th due to a transfer process alarm. TEPCO identified the alarm as being caused by an abnormality in the valve between the treated water tank and the transfer pump, replaced the valve, and resumed the discharge at 4:10 p.m. on the 11th. Just two days later, on the 13th at 5:04 p.m., the discharge was automatically halted for the second time. (도쿄전력은 지난 1일 20차 방류를 시작했으나, 10일 오후 4시 17분 이송 공정 경보가 발생해 방류가 자동으로 정지됐다. 도쿄전력은 오염수 수조와 이송 펌프 사이 밸브의 이상으로 경보가 울린 것으로 파악하고 밸브를 교체한 뒤 11일 오후 4시 10분 재개했다. 이로부터 이틀 만인 13일 오후 5시 4분 방류가 두 번째로 자동 정지됐던 것이다.)

item.title: North Korea Reacts to Korea-EU Statement as "Sovereignty Infringement"... Blue House Says "Pursuing Peaceful Coexistence with a Long-Term Perspective" (北, 한·EU 성명에 “주권침해” 반발...靑 “긴 안목으로 평화공존 추진”)
item.description:
North Korea Reacts to Korea-EU Statement as "Sovereignty Infringement"... Blue House Says "Pursuing Peaceful Coexistence with a Long-Term Perspective" (北, 한·EU 성명에 “주권침해” 반발...靑 “긴 안목으로 평화공존 추진”)

In response to North Korea's objection that the joint statement issued by South Korea and the European Union (EU) on the 10th (local time) constitutes a "sovereignty infringement," the Blue House stated on the 14th, "The government will consistently pursue a policy of peaceful coexistence on the Korean Peninsula with a long-term perspective." The Blue House added that "the EU also supports our government's policy for easing tensions and establishing peace on the Korean Peninsula." <<> President Lee Jae-myung, currently on a European tour, held a summit at the EU headquarters in Brussels, Belgium on the 10th and issued the "Korea-EU Summit Joint Statement." The joint statement included a "strong condemnation of the illegal military cooperation between Russia and North Korea" regarding North Korea's troop dispatch to Russia. It also stated that "North Korea will never be recognized as a nuclear weapons state under the NPT (Non-Proliferation Treaty)" and demanded that "North Korea allow access to international and humanitarian organizations" to improve the human rights situation in North Korea. <<> This marks the first time under the current government that such strong criticism, including "condemnation," has been directed at North Korea. It is known that the EU strongly pushed for the wording of this joint statement. However, the Blue House stated that "there is nothing new," saying it merely reaffirmed "content that South Korea has already publicly stated to the international community." <<> Nevertheless, North Korea strongly reacted by issuing a statement under the name of the "Spokesperson of the 10th Bureau of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs" with the title "South Korea is an Invariable Enemy Nation Inherently Hostile and Confrontational." The 10th Bureau of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs handles affairs related to South Korea. <<> In its statement, North Korea said, "They issued a joint statement filled with provocative phrases such as 'illegal' and they will never 'recognize' our exercise of sovereign rights, including our status as a nuclear weapons state and military cooperation with Russia (North Korea-Russia), and they 'strongly condemn' it," adding, "This is a clear infringement on our state's sovereignty and a grave hostile act." <<> North Korea continued, "(South Korea) has essentially thrown away the sham signs it has tirelessly touted, such as 'respect for the system' and 'non-pursuit of hostile acts,'" and "South Korea's ruler has cast off the mask of 'peace' that he had been awkwardly wearing." <<> North Korea stated, "Beyond hostility toward our country, the primary enemy nation that can never be allowed to exist, and the 'dagger' of the United States for invading Joseon and the Asian continent—this is the true nature and destiny of South Korea," and "Regardless of what the Seoul authorities say or do, it becomes a challenge to us, and our principle of treating South Korea as a thoroughgoing hostile nation remains unchanged." (청와대는 한국과 유럽연합(EU)이 지난 10일(현지 시각) 발표한 공동성명에 북한이 “주권 침해”라고 반발한 데 대해, 14일 “정부는 긴 안목을 가지고 한반도 평화공존 정책을 일관되게 추진할 것”이라는 입장을 밝혔다. 청와대는 “EU도 한반도의 긴장 완화와 평화 정착을 위한 우리 정부의 정책을 지지한다”고 했다.)

item.title: The Homework Left by a Split Ballot Box… Is It Time to Revise the Early Voting System? (갈라진 투표함이 남긴 숙제…사전투표제 손볼 때 됐나)
item.description:
The Homework Left by a Split Ballot Box… Is It Time to Revise the Early Voting System? (갈라진 투표함이 남긴 숙제…사전투표제 손볼 때 됐나 )

This Seoul mayoral election’s scriptless comeback victory starkly reveals a divide in voter sentiment based on voting methods. In early votes opened first in many regions, Democratic Party candidate Jung Won-oh (64.3%) nearly doubled People Power Party candidate Oh Se-hoon (32.9%), but as the election-day ballot boxes—where Oh (59.1%) significantly outpaced Jung (38.3%)—were opened, the gap reversed. (이번 서울시장 선거의 각본 없는 역전승은 투표 방식에 따른 표심 단절을 극명하게 보여준다. 다수 지역에서 먼저 개봉된 사전투표에서는 정원오 더불어민주당 후보(64.3%)가 오세훈 국민의힘 후보(32.9%)를 두 배 가까이 압도했지만, 오 후보(59.1%)가 정 후보(38.3%)를 크게 이긴 본투표함이 열리면서 격차가 뒤집혔다.)

Even in the 2014 local elections, when early voting was first introduced for nationwide elections, the difference between early and election-day voting results was not as pronounced as it is now. At that time, in the Seoul mayoral election, the vote shares for candidates Park Won-soon and Chung Mong-joon were similar between early voting (59.4% vs. 39.7%) and election-day voting (55.4% vs. 43.8%). (사전투표가 전국 단위 선거에서 처음 도입된 2014년 지방선거만 해도 사전투표와 본투표의 결과 차이는 지금처럼 크지 않았다. 당시 서울시장 선거에서 박원순 후보와 정몽준 후보의 득표율은 사전투표(59.4% 대 39.7%)와 본투표(55.4% 대 43.8%)가 비슷했다.)

However, the complete reversal of early and election-day voting results in this local election is no coincidence. In a May JoongAng Ilbo survey of Seoul voters, when asked, “When do you plan to vote?” the progressive group favored early voting (54%) by a majority, while the conservative group overwhelmingly favored election-day voting (70%). (그런데 이번 지방선거에서 사전투표와 본투표 결과가 정반대로 나타난 것은 우연이 아니다. 지난 5월 서울 유권자를 대상으로 한 중앙일보 조사에서 ‘언제 투표할 예정인가’라는 질문에 진보층은 사전투표(54%)가 과반을 차지한 반면, 보수층은 본투표(70%)가 압도적으로 높았다.)

Starkly Different Turnout by Early and Election-Day Voting (사전투표와 본투표별로 극명한 투표율)

Looking at the timeline, the divide based on voters’ ideological leanings becomes even clearer. In a YTN survey just before the 2017 presidential election, intentions for early voting were comparable among progressives (25%) and conservatives (22%). But in a survey by the three major broadcasters during the 2022 presidential election, progressives’ intention to vote early soared to 42%, while conservatives remained at 23%, signaling the onset of a “divide by date.” (시계열 추이를 보면 유권자 이념성향별 단절 현상은 더욱 명확하다. 2017년 대선 직전 YTN 조사에선 사전투표 의향이 진보층 25%, 보수층 22%로 대등했다. 하지만 2022년 대선 당시 지상파 3사 조사에선 진보층의 사전투표 의향이 42%로 폭등한 반면, 보수층은 23%에 머물며 ‘날짜별 갈라치기’의 서막을 알렸다.)

Election experts point to the 2020 general election as a key turning point. Allegations of election fraud raised by hardline YouTubers and some politicians shortly after the Democratic Party’s landslide victory of 180 seats—regardless of their factual validity—significantly impacted voter behavior. As a result, the dichotomy of “early voting for progressives, election-day voting for conservatives” took hold, and has now become embedded as a political culture. (선거전문가들은 2020년 총선을 중요한 분기점으로 꼽는다. 민주당이 180석 압승을 거둔 직후 강경 유튜버와 일부 정치인이 제기한 부정선거 의혹은 실체적 진위를 떠나 유권자의 투표 행태에 적지 않은 영향을 미쳤다. 그 결과 ‘사전투표는 진보, 본투표는 보수’라는 이분법 공식이 생겼고, 이제는 하나의 정치문화로 자리 잡았다.)

Elections are said to be a festival of democracy, but in our society today, they are mired in suspicion and distrust. At the center of this is the early voting system. A clear line must be drawn here: pointing out the flaws of early voting does not mean endorsing election fraud conspiracy theories like “ballot box swapping” or “digital manipulation.” Quite the opposite. The urgent task now is not a wasteful political battle over the truth of conspiracy theories, but designing a system that the vast majority of the public can accept without a shred of doubt. (선거는 민주주의의 축제라지만 오늘날 우리 사회에서 선거는 의혹과 불신에 휩싸여 있다. 그 중심에 사전투표제가 있다. 여기서 분명히 선을 그어둘 대목이 있다. 사전투표제의 맹점을 지적하는 것이 결코 ‘투표함 바꿔치기’나 ‘전산 조작’ 같은 부정선거 음모론에 동조하는 것을 의미하진 않는다. 오히려 그 반대다. 지금 시급한 과제는 음모론의 진위를 둘러싼 소모적 정쟁이 아니라, 국민 다수가 한 치의 의심 없이 수용할 수 있는 제도를 설계하는 일이다.)

We must also be wary of branding calls for abolishing or reforming early voting as mere “election fraud conspiracy theories.” Such an approach can suppress even reasonable criticism of the system, fueling greater distrust. (사전투표 폐지나 개편을 주장하는 목소리를 무조건 ‘부정선거 음모론’으로 몰아세우는 낙인찍기도 경계해야 한다. 그런 접근은 제도에 대한 합리적인 문제 제기마저 봉쇄해 더 큰 불신을 키울 수 있다.)

The rationale behind the early voting system, introduced in 2012 under bipartisan agreement in a National Assembly where the Saenuri Party held a majority, was clear. It aimed to boost turnout by guaranteeing voting rights for those unable to vote on election day. This is evidenced by the numbers. The early voting rate rose from 11.5% in the 2014 local elections to 23.5% in this one, and the final turnout also increased from 56.8% to 61.0%. Solely in terms of expanding quantitative participation, early voting is a successful policy. (2012년 새누리당이 다수당이던 국회에서 여야 합의로 도입한 사전투표제의 명분은 확실했다. 본투표일에 투표가 어려운 이들의 참정권을 보장해 투표율을 높이자는 취지였다. 지표상으로도 증명된다. 2014년 지방선거 당시 11.5%였던 사전투표율은 이번 지방선거에서 23.5%로 상승했고, 최종 투표율도 56.8%에서 61.0%로 높아졌다. 양적 참여 확대라는 측면만 놓고 보면 사전투표는 성공적인 정책이다.)

The problem lies not in turnout, but in the shift in the political nature of the act of voting itself. Somewhere along the way, the timing of a vote has become not just a matter of schedule but a signal reflecting political identity. That support leans one way or another depending on which day one votes creates a subtle pressure, as it can inadvertently reveal to those around whom one voted for. (문제는 투표율이 아니라 투표 행위가 갖는 정치적 성격의 변질이다. 언제부턴가 투표 시기는 단순한 스케줄의 선택이 아니라 정치적 정체성을 반영하는 신호가 되고 있다. 어느 날짜에 투표하느냐로 지지 성향이 갈리다 보니, 누구를 찍었는지가 주변에 은연중에 드러날 수도 있다는 묘한 압박감을 준다.)

The fact that these two voter groups vote under different information environments is also a serious issue. Unlike early voters, election-day voters can factor in the final issues that arise in the last three days before making a decision. An election should ideally be a process of asking all voters their opinion under as equal conditions as possible, but as the share of early voting grows, information inequality among voters increases. (두 유권자 집단이 서로 다른 정보 환경에서 투표한다는 점도 심각한 문제다. 사전투표자와 달리 본투표자는 마지막 사흘간 발생한 최종 이슈까지 반영해 판단할 수 있다. 선거는 가급적 동일한 조건에서 모든 유권자에게 의사를 묻는 과정이어야 하지만, 사전투표 비중이 커질수록 유권자 간 정보 불평등이 커진다.)

The growing proportion of early voting is also undermining the accuracy of exit polls. Broadcasters calculate their final predictions for election day by adding demographic weights for early voters to the exit poll results. The wider the gap in sentiment between the two groups, the greater the burden of statistical correction. The confusion following the inaccurate exit polls right after the June 3 local elections is a testament to this. (사전투표 비중 확대는 출구조사의 정확성도 흔들고 있다. 방송사들은 본투표 당일 실시한 출구조사 결과에 사전투표자의 인구통계학적 가중치를 더해 최종 예측치를 산출한다. 양측의 표심 격차가 벌어질수록 통계적 보정의 부담이 커질 수밖에 없다. 6·3 지방선거 직후 출구조사가 어긋나며 빚어진 혼란도 그 방증이다.)

The cost of suspicion and conflict arising from storing and moving early ballot boxes for days is also significant. Regardless of whether election fraud actually occurred, the very situation where the electoral system itself is constantly questioned by the public represents a massive loss for democracy. (사전투표함을 며칠씩 보관하고 옮기는 과정에서 생겨나는 의혹과 갈등의 비용도 만만치 않다. 실제로 부정선거가 저질러졌느냐의 진위와 상관없이, 선거제도 자체가 끊임없이 국민에게 의심을 받는 상황 그 자체가 민주주의의 막대한 손실이다.)

Trust is More Important Than Voting Convenience (투표 편의성보다 중요한 건 신뢰)

Of course, arguments in favor of early voting are also compelling. For voters with unavoidable circumstances like shift workers or those on business trips or vacations, early voting provides a practical means of participation. However, democracy must pursue both values of convenience and reliability. Neither can be emphasized alone. (물론 사전투표 옹호론도 충분히 설득력이 있다. 교대근무자나 출장·여행자처럼 불가피한 사정이 있는 유권자에게 사전투표는 실질적인 참여 수단이다. 그러나 민주주의는 편의성과 신뢰성이라는 두 가치를 함께 추구해야 한다. 어느 한쪽만 강조할 수는 없다.)

Overseas examples are worth considering. France holds major elections like the presidential one on Sundays, and Germany holds federal parliamentary elections on Sundays or public holidays to boost participation. Taiwan operates on the principle of on-site voting on election day without early voting, maintaining social trust in the vote-counting results. The key point is that each country optimizes its system according to its own political culture and level of trust. (해외 사례도 참고할 만하다. 프랑스는 대선 등 주요 선거를 일요일에 실시하고, 독일은 연방의회 선거를 일요일 또는 공휴일에 치르면서 참여율을 높인다. 대만은 선거 당일 현장투표를 원칙으로 운영하며 사전투표 없이 개표 결과에 대한 사회적 신뢰를 지켜낸다. 핵심은 각 나라가 자국의 정치문화와 신뢰 수준에 맞춰 제도를 최적화하고 있다는 점이다.)

We could also consider changing election day to a weekend, or extending it to two or three days by designating the last day as a holiday. This approach could lower participation barriers—the original goal of early voting—while ensuring all voters vote in the same information environment and blocking the structural grounds for suspicion associated with long-term storage and transportation. It would also leave no room for partisan advantage or disadvantage. (우리도 본투표일을 주말로 바꾸거나 2~3일로 늘려 마지막 하루를 휴일로 지정하는 방식을 검토해볼 수 있다. 이 방안은 사전투표가 해결하려던 참여 장벽을 낮추면서도 모든 유권자가 동일한 정보 환경에서 투표하고, 장기 보관·이송 과정의 의혹 구조도 차단할 수 있다. 특정 정당에 유불리가 개입할 여지도 없다.)

The reality revealed in a February 2025 Weekly Chosun poll, where opinions for and against early voting were evenly split at 50%, shows that public consensus on the system’s legitimacy is weak. Calls for reform of the early voting system are distinct from the extreme agitation of some conspiracy theorists. They should be understood as aiming to secure electoral transparency by correcting structural flaws that provide fodder for distrust. In elections, as important as the number of voters is whether everyone can accept the outcome. What our society now needs to ponder is not voting convenience, but complete trust in the election process. (2025년 2월 주간조선 여론조사에서 사전투표제 찬반이 50%로 팽팽하게 갈린 현실은, 제도의 정당성에 대해 국민적 합의가 취약하다는 방증이다. 사전투표제에 대한 개선론은 일부 음모론자들의 극단적 선동과 궤를 달리한다. 불신의 빌미를 제공하는 구조적 맹점을 바로잡아 선거의 투명성을 확보하려는 목적으로 이해해야 한다. 선거에서 투표자 수만큼이나 중요한 것은 결과를 모두가 승복할 수 있느냐다. 지금 우리 사회가 고민해야 할 것은 투표의 편의성이 아니라 선거에 대한 온전한 신뢰다.)

item.title: An Election Without Winners, Only Losers: Jang Dong-hyeok’s ‘Mental Victory’ and Jeong Cheong-rae’s ‘Ddal Victory’ (승장 없이 패장들만 남은 선거… 장동혁은 ‘정신 승리’, 정청래는 ‘개딸 승리’)
item.description:
An Election Without Winners, Only Losers: Jang Dong-hyeok’s ‘Mental Victory’ and Jeong Cheong-rae’s ‘Ddal Victory’ (승장 없이 패장들만 남은 선거… 장동혁은 ‘정신 승리’, 정청래는 ‘개딸 승리’)

Following the June 3rd by-elections, the leaders of both the ruling and opposition parties have been plunged into a quagmire of collective responsibility for their election defeats. Democratic Party leader Jeong Cheong-rae is facing fierce criticism after suffering comeback defeats in key battlegrounds such as Seoul, Daegu, and Busan. Within the pro-Moon Jae-in faction, calls are growing for him to “resign immediately” and “not run in the party convention.” People Power Party leader Jang Dong-hyeok is also under pressure from all sides to step down. The argument is that losing 12 out of 16 metropolitan and provincial government seats is Jang’s fault for failing to break away from the ‘Yoon again’ strategy and focusing solely on maintaining his party leadership, hence the demand to “take responsibility and step down.” <<> Leaders of minor parties have also either tasted the bitter cup of defeat or suffered major blows to their leadership due to disastrous election results. Cho Kuk, former leader of the Rebuilding Korea Party, ran in Gyeonggi Pyeongtaek-eul but came in third and lost. He ultimately stepped down from the party leadership, taking responsibility for the defeat. Progressive Party co-chair Kim Jae-yeon also lost in Pyeongtaek-eul, finishing last among five candidates. The Reform Party received its worst-ever scorecard, with only one Hwaseong City council member elected out of about 190 candidates. This has significantly weakened Lee Jun-seok’s leadership and presence. <<> As a result, the June 3rd elections are being called a ‘graveyard for party leaders.’ There are no election winners, only losers. The sense of responsibility is correspondingly large. This is due to the unexpected and delicate election outcome, where neither the ruling nor opposition party can claim victory. The opposition lost numerically, while the ruling party lost in key battlegrounds. Party leaders who personally ran also faced defeat. Not only are their leadership positions threatened, but their political careers are now at stake. <<> Amidst the pressure to resign, Jeong Cheong-rae is seeking a breakthrough by holding a general meeting of lawmakers and visiting the Honam region. He aims to run again at the August party convention to retain his position as the ruling party’s leader. Despite intense scrutiny from the pro-Moon faction and falling approval ratings, Jeong’s ace in the hole is the hard-line party supporters, known as ‘Ddal.’ He plans to rally their support to turn the tide. <<> Jang Dong-hyeok is countering the ‘responsibility for election defeat’ narrative with a ‘strong performance’ argument. He claims that since the party performed well in many areas and won in key battlegrounds, he should not be called a loser. Internal reformists criticize this as “a mental victory and a case of the pot calling the kettle black.” However, Jang’s strategy is to use the hard-line support base and the pro-Yoon leadership as a shield to hold onto his party power. This is being described as a ‘mental victory-style holding pattern.’ Will the two leaders’ efforts to retain their power succeed? <<> After elections, the joy and sorrow of winners and losers typically diverge sharply. A winning party leader sees approval ratings rise and becomes a strong contender for the next top nomination. The loser, however, faces leadership instability and pressure to resign. This time, both the ruling and opposition party leaders are subject to this responsibility debate, which is highly unusual. <<> Democratic Party leader Jeong Cheong-rae is cornered by the election defeat in Seoul and the Yeongnam region. Pro-Moon lawmakers within the party and those from Honam are pressuring Jeong daily to take responsibility for the battleground loss and resign. The same applies to People Power Party leader Jang Dong-hyeok. Internal reformists criticize Jang for lacking the qualification to lead, arguing the party lost the local elections due to his ‘Yoon again’ line and regressive leadership. <<> Cho Kuk, former leader of the Rebuilding Korea Party, failed in his bid for Gyeonggi Pyeongtaek-eul by-election, coming in third. He resigned as party leader immediately after the election, taking responsibility for the loss. Reform Party leader Lee Jun-seok also suffered a major blow to his leadership from the near-failing election performance. Only one out of 190 candidates for metropolitan, basic, and local council positions won a seat, a Hwaseong City council member. Progressive Party co-chair Kim Jae-yeon also ran in Pyeongtaek-eul but finished last among five candidates. This situation has led to the June 3rd elections being dubbed a ‘graveyard for party leaders.’ <<> This is indirectly confirmed by opinion polls. According to a Media Tomato survey, when asked, ‘Which party leader is the biggest loser?’, Jang Dong-hyeok received the most responses at 30.3%, followed by Jeong Cheong-rae at 25.6%, former leader Cho Kuk at 11.8%, and Lee Jun-seok at 4.4%. Notably, supporters of both the PPP and DP rated their own party leader as a bigger loser than the opposition leader, indicating significant dissatisfaction within their own ranks. <<> This phenomenon stems from the unexpected and finely balanced outcome of the June 3rd elections, where neither side can claim victory. Overall, the ruling party had the edge, but in key battlegrounds like Seoul, Daegu, Gyeongnam, and Gyeonggi Pyeongtaek-eul, the PPP staged dramatic late comebacks. The opposition lost on the numbers, while the ruling party lost psychologically. <<> There was also significant criticism of errors and unfavorable sentiment toward both party leaders. Jeong Cheong-rae sparked a major controversy with his “Oppa, give it a try” remark, and faced blame for the defeat in Yeongnam. Internal party strife surrounding nominations was also severe, such as Gwangju Mayor Kim Gwan-yeong running as an independent in Jeonbuk. Jang Dong-hyeok’s ‘Yoon again’ line and regressive behavior invited a backlash against the ruling party. It was observed that wherever Jang campaigned, the party lost. <<> Power struggles for party leadership within both the ruling and opposition parties also amplify the responsibility debate. The DP is approaching its August 17th party convention. The pro-Moon faction, with potential leadership candidates like former Prime Minister Kim Min-seok and former leader Song Young-gil, has begun intensive scrutiny of Jeong Cheong-rae. They emphasize the election responsibility issue to attack him. In the PPP, Jang Dong-hyeok’s ‘hold on to power at all costs’ behavior is escalating the conflict. <<> The DP’s pro-Moon faction is repeatedly calling for Jeong Cheong-rae’s resignation. In his opening remarks at a general meeting of lawmakers on the 11th, Jeong called for “unity.” Contrary to his expectations, however, the pro-Moon faction then unleashed a barrage of criticism regarding responsibility for the election defeat. Jeong spent 70 minutes listening to this critique. <<> Jeong had previously stated, “The people are eternal, and the government is short-lived,” which sparked strong backlash from the pro-Moon faction. He then pivoted to a Loki-like strategy of avoiding confrontation. However, the pro-Moon faction continued to criticize him on the 12th with the retort, “Party members are eternal, and party leadership is short-lived.” <<> It is reported that Jeong plans to resign later this month. However, this is framed not as being forced out, but as resigning in time to declare his candidacy for the party leadership. The strategy appears to be to step away from the immediate storm to rally support from pro-Chung Cheong-rae and pro-Moon factions, as well as hard-line party members, from an outside position. This is based on the judgment that, under attack from the pro-Moon faction, his only reliable base is the hard-line support represented by the ‘Ddal.’ He believes appealing to these hard-line supporters, who hold hegemony within the party, is key to victory. <<> Jeong visited the May 18th National Cemetery in Gwangju on the 12th and held an on-site Supreme Council meeting to appease some Honam voters who turned against him in this election. The nomination controversy cost the party several seats in Jeonnam and Jeonbuk, where they lost to independents and the Rebuilding Korea Party. Meanwhile, Jeong announced, “We will completely abolish the supplementary investigation powers of the prosecution,” a clear policy stance aimed at courting the hard-line support base. <<> However, there are observations that Jeong’s path to reelection as party leader is not necessarily bright. Some polls show him trailing not only former Prime Minister Kim Min-seok but also former leader Song Young-gil among DP supporters. Support for Jeong was high before the election, but the tide appears to have shifted. Some even suggest he might withdraw his candidacy. The argument is that with anti-Jeong Cheong-rae sentiment spreading not only among general party supporters but also in the crucial Honam region, a second term will be difficult this time. <<> However, Jeong’s camp argues, “In the last party convention, general polls showed a close race with former lawmaker Park Chan-dae, but Jeong won a landslide with the support of hard-line party members. Given time, the support from party members will recover.” The key will be how quickly he can restore his leadership, damaged by the Seoul election defeat and the Jeonbuk nomination controversy. <<> Jang Dong-hyeok is also facing intense internal pressure to resign. However, Jang shows no sign of backing down. Instead, he argues, “Look at the election results. We performed well.” and “The Democratic Party is the one that claims defeat, so why do people within our party say we lost?” He insists it was a ‘winning election’ and thus there is no reason for him to step down. <<> Reformists criticize him for “cherry-picking advantageous indicators and making baseless claims.” They say Jang alone is engaged in a groundless ‘mental victory.’ In response, Jang retorts that it is not his mental victory but the adversary’s mental defeat. <<> Younger lawmakers plan to intensify pressure on Jang to resign while waging a public opinion campaign. They have communicated this intention to floor leader Jeong Jeom-sik. Jeong seems inclined to reflect for a few more days and observe public sentiment before deciding. Currently, it appears a majority of lawmakers favor Jang’s resignation. However, some lawmakers from the Yeongnam region express concern that “there is no way to force Jang to resign” and that “doing so could only escalate the conflict.” <<> Jang seems intent on breaking through the resignation calls by pushing for a re-election due to the voting interruption incident. His logic is that this is not the time for a resignation controversy when young people are exercising their voting rights. However, the majority of lawmakers oppose his call for a full re-election, calling it unrealistic and unpersuasive. There is also significant concern that he might be trying to ride the conspiracy theories about election fraud under the pretext of a re-election. <<> Jang is currently resisting resignation pressure by using the pro-Yoon leadership and hard-line support base, which are favorable to him, as a shield. Whether Jang’s stubbornness will prevail or the reformists, leveraging public opinion, will succeed in shaking his position remains to be seen. (이번 6·3 선거 이후 여야 각 당 대표들이 선거 패배에 따른 집단 책임론의 수렁에 빠졌습니다. 민주당 정청래 대표는 서울·대구·부산 등 격전지에서 역전패를 당하면서 거센 공격을 받고 있습니다. 친명계에선 “당장 사퇴하라” “전당대회에 불출마하라”는 비판을 쏟아내고 있습니다. 국민의힘 장동혁 대표도 전방위 사퇴 압박을 받고 있습니다. 광역단체장 16곳 중 12곳을 진 것은 ‘윤 어게인’과 결별하지 못한 채 당권 유지에만 골몰한 장 대표의 잘못이므로 “책임지고 물러나라”는 것입니다.)

item.title: President Lee Visits Florence, Signs MOU for Cooperation with Uffizi Gallery (피렌체 찾은 李대통령...우피치미술관과 협력 MOU 체결)
item.description:
President Lee Visits Florence, Signs MOU for Cooperation with Uffizi Gallery (피렌체 찾은 李대통령...우피치미술관과 협력 MOU 체결)

President Lee Jae-myung, on a state visit to Italy, visited Florence, the capital of the Tuscany region in northern Italy, on the 13th (local time). The President met with Tuscany Governor Eugenio Giani over lunch and discussed ways to expand cultural exchange and cooperation between the two countries. He also visited the Uffizi Gallery. On the occasion of President Lee's visit, the National Museum of Korea signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the Uffizi Gallery to revitalize mutual cooperation, including the exchange of exhibits. (이탈리아를 국빈 방문 중인 이재명 대통령은 13일(현지 시각) 이탈리아 북부 토스카나의 주도 피렌체를 방문했다. 이 대통령은 에우제니오 쟈니 토스카나 주지사와 오찬을 겸해 만나 양국 간 문화 교류·협력 확대 방안을 논의했고, 우피치 미술관을 방문했다. 이 대통령의 방문을 계기로, 국립중앙박물관은 우피치 미술관과 전시품 교류 등 상호 협력을 활성화하는 내용의 양해각서(MOU)를 체결했다.)

During his meeting with Governor Giani, President Lee mentioned the 'Florence Korean Film Festival,' which marks its 24th year this year. According to the presidential office, the President said, "Tuscany, the birthplace and cradle of the Renaissance and home to the world-renowned Uffizi Gallery, has been showcasing the artistry and quality of Korean cinema to Europe and the global stage through the Florence Korean Film Festival since 2003." He requested continued interest and support to establish it as an international cultural festival representing Tuscany. President Lee also asked the Florence city government to pay special attention to improving convenience and ensuring public safety for Korean citizens visiting Florence. (이 대통령은 이날 쟈니 주지사를 만나 올해로 24년 차를 맞은 ‘피렌체 한국 영화제’를 언급했다. 이 대통령은 “르네상스가 탄생하고 발전한 고장이자 세계적인 우피치 미술관을 보유한 토스카나가 2003년부터 피렌체 한국영화제를 통해 한국 영화의 예술성과 작품성을 유럽과 세계무대에 선보여오고 있다”면서, 토스카나를 대표하는 국제 문화 축제로 자리매김할 수 있도록 지속적인 관심과 지원을 당부했다고 청와대는 전했다. 이 대통령은 피렌체를 방문하는 우리 국민의 편의 증진과 치안 확보에 대한 피렌체 시정부의 각별한 관심도 요청했다.)

In response, Governor Giani reportedly said that he had read President Lee's autobiography with deep impression and expressed hope that the President, having overcome the difficult hardships of a child laborer and become a human rights lawyer, would play a major role not only in Korean democracy but also in the advancement of democracy in the international community. (이에 쟈니 주지사는 이 대통령의 자서전을 감명 깊게 읽었다면서, 소년공의 어려운 역경을 딛고 인권 변호사로 한국 민주주의는 물론 국제사회의 민주주의 발전을 위해서도 큰 역할을 할 것으로 기대된다고 답했다고 한다.)

After the meeting with Governor Giani, President Lee visited the Uffizi Gallery and viewed representative works such as Giotto's 'Ognissanti Madonna,' Botticelli's 'The Birth of Venus,' and Leonardo da Vinci's 'Annunciation.' (이 대통령은 쟈니 주지사 면담 뒤엔 우피치 미술관을 찾아, 대표 작품인 조토의 ‘오니 산티 마돈나’, 보티첼리의 ‘비너스의 탄생’, 레오나르도 다빈치의 ‘수태고지’ 등을 관람했다.)

National Museum of Korea Director Yoon Hong-geun and Uffizi Gallery Director Simone Verde signed an MOU on cooperation in museum programs and services. The MOU includes provisions to enhance exchanges in areas such as exhibition, interpretation, and education, including the loan of collection items, as well as collection management, restoration, and publishing. (유홍준 국립중앙박물관장과 시모네 베르데 우피치 미술관장은 ‘박물관 프로그램 및 서비스 분야 협력에 관한 MOU’를 체결했다. MOU에는 양측이 소장품 대여를 포함한 전시·해설·교육, 소장품 관리와 복원·출판 등 분야에서 교류를 증진하는 내용이 포함됐다.)

The presidential office explained that President Lee's visit to Florence was in line with the customary protocol for state guests by the Italian government. This practice involves foreign heads of state on official visits to Italy touring provincial cities outside the capital, Rome. The presidential office noted that the decision to choose Florence as the President's destination was based on factors such as it being the Italian provincial city most visited by Korean tourists. (청와대는 이 대통령의 피렌체 방문이, 이탈리아 정부의 국빈에 대한 예우 관례에 따른 것이라고 설명했다. 이탈리아를 국빈 방문하는 외국 정상이, 수도인 로마 외에 이탈리아의 지방 도시를 방문하는 관례를 따랐다는 것이다. 청와대는 피렌체가 한국 관광객이 가장 많이 찾는 이탈리아 지방 도시라는 점 등을 감안해 이 대통령의 방문지를 결정했다고 설명했다.)

item.title: DJ and Kono's ‘Bond of Mutual Trust’...A Private Breakfast Alone the Day After the President’s Inauguration (DJ 와 고노의 ‘간담상조’...대통령 취임 다음날 단둘이 조찬)
item.description:
DJ and Kono's ‘Bond of Mutual Trust’...A Private Breakfast Alone the Day After the President’s Inauguration (DJ 와 고노의 ‘간담상조’...대통령 취임 다음날 단둘이 조찬 )

<<>> Yohei Kono, the former Speaker of the Japanese House of Representatives who played a key role in the ‘Kono Statement’ acknowledging the Japanese government’s responsibility for the wartime comfort women issue, passed away on the 8th. He was 89 years old. ()

Japanese media did not treat his death as the mere passing of an elderly politician. Major newspapers such as Yomiuri, Asahi, and Mainichi praised him as a great statesman who emphasized relations with South Korea and China in post-war Japanese politics. To South Koreans, Kono is remembered for the ‘Kono Statement’ issued in 1993. This statement, which acknowledged the Japanese government's involvement in the mobilization of comfort women and expressed an apology, laid the foundation for South Korea-Japan reconciliation that later led to the 1998 Kim Dae-jung-Obuchi Joint Declaration. (일제 시대 위안부 문제에 대해 일본 정부의 책임을 인정한 ‘고노 담화’의 주역 고노 요헤이 전 일본 중의원 의장이 8일 별세했습니다. 향년 89세였습니다.)

A Politician Familiar to South Koreans Through the Kono Statement (일본 언론은 그의 죽음을 단순한 원로 정치인의 별세로 다루지 않았습니다. 요미우리, 아사히, 마이니치 등 주요 신문들 그가 전후 일본 정치에서 한국, 중국과의 관계를 강조한 큰 정치가라고 평가했습니다. 한국인들에게 고노는 1993년 발표된 ‘고노 담화’로 기억됩니다. 일본 정부가 위안부 동원 과정에 관여했다는 사실을 인정하고 사죄의 뜻을 밝힌 이 담화는 훗날 1998년 김대중-오부치 공동선언으로 이어지는 한일 화해의 토대를 마련했습니다.)

I, too, came to know him through the Kono Statement. I first learned of him in 1999 while covering the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade as a political reporter for the Chosun Ilbo, and during my time as a Tokyo correspondent, I wrote several articles about him and his son, Taro Kono (who served as Foreign Minister and Defense Minister). However, as time passed, what left the most lasting impression on me was his special relationship with former President Kim Dae-jung. (고노 담화로 한국인에게 친숙한 정치인)

I believe that the deep relationship between the two men, spanning from the 1970s, laid the groundwork for South Korea-Japan reconciliation. The Nikkei newspaper, in commemorating Kono’s death, described his relationship with DJ as ‘간담상조 (肝膽相照)’, a fitting expression, I think. Though of different nationalities, they shared a relationship of deep trust, opening their hearts to each other, worthy of the idiom meaning “to bare one’s liver and gall to each other.” (저 역시 고노 담화를 통해 그를 알게 됐습니다. 1999년 조선일보 정치부 기자로 외교통상부를 담당하면서 처음 그를 알게 됐고, 도쿄 특파원 시절에는 그와 그의 아들 고노 다로 의원(외무상, 방위상 역임)과 관련된 기사를 여러 차례 썼습니다. 그런데 시간이 흐를수록 제게 가장 인상적으로 남은 것은 그와 김대중 전 대통령의 특별한 관계였습니다.)

In his lifetime, Kono introduced Japan's foreign policy and related anecdotes in his book ‘Frank Words on Japanese Diplomacy - Recollections and Suggestions’. In this 2015 book, he detailed his connection with DJ and their untold stories. Kono deepened his bond with DJ by taking the lead in the campaign to save his life in Japan’s political circles following the 1973 Kim Dae-jung kidnapping incident. Over the decades that followed, their relationship evolved beyond political exchange into one of trust. This book contains several previously little-known scenes. (저는 70년대부터 이어진 두 사람의 깊은 관계에 의해서 한일 화해의 토대가 마련됐다고 생각합니다. 일본경제신문이 고노의 별세를 추모하면서 DJ와의 관계를 ‘간담상조(肝膽相照)’라고 했는데, 적절한 표현이라고 생각합니다. 두 사람은 국적은 달랐지만, 간과 쓸개를 서로 꺼내 비춰본다는 고사성어에 걸맞게 속마음을 털어놓으며 깊이 신뢰하는 관계였습니다.)

[Scene 1] Dining Alone Without an Interpreter the Day After DJ’s Inauguration (고노는 생전에 ‘일본 외교에 대한 직언-회상과 제언’이라는 책을 통해 일본의 외교 정책 및 자신이 관련된 비화를 소개했습니다. 그는 2015년 출간된 이 책에서 DJ와의 인연과 비사를 상세히 소개했습니다. 고노는 1973년 김대중 납치 사건 당시 일본 정계에서 그에 대한 구명운동에 앞장서면서 인연을 깊게 만들었습니다. 이후 수십 년 동안 두 사람의 관계는 정치적 교류를 넘어 신뢰 관계로 발전했습니다. 이 책에 지금까지 잘 알려지지 않은 장면이 여러 차례 나옵니다.)

Among them, a little-known scene occurred right after President Kim Dae-jung’s inauguration in February 1998. Attending the inauguration ceremony from Japan were former Prime Ministers Yasuhiro Nakasone and Noboru Takeshita, along with Kono, a former Foreign Minister. Kono noted, “The two former prime ministers seemed not to understand why I was invited.” The bond built between the two men since DJ’s kidnapping incident was not well-known in Japan. The morning after the inauguration, they had a private meal together at the Blue House with no interpreter or secretary present. It was unprecedented for a South Korean president to have a private, unpublicized meal alone with a former Japanese cabinet minister the day after his inauguration. President Kim, receiving his heartfelt congratulations, told him that they would now firmly build South Korea-Japan relations. ([장면 1] DJ 취임식 다음 날 통역 없이 단둘이 식사 )

Kono recalled, “We had met many times in Tokyo, but the first time I met him in Seoul was this meeting with President Kim. Knowing the long years of hardship he had endured, it felt like a dream.” They discussed the future of South Korea-Japan relations like old friends. (그 중에서도 지금까지 잘 알려지지 않은 장면은 1998년 2월 김대중 대통령 취임 직후 있었습니다. 김 대통령 취임식에 일본에서는 총리를 지낸 나카소네 야스히로, 다케시타 노보루와 외무상을 지낸 고노가 참석했습니다. 고노는 “두 전직 총리는 왜 내가 초청받았는지 이해하지 못하는 것 같았다”고 기록했습니다. DJ 납치사건 이후, 쌓아온 두 사람의 인연이 일본에 잘 알려지지 않았던 겁니다. 고노는 취임식 다음날 아침 청와대에서 통역도, 비서관도 없이 단둘이 식사를 함께 했습니다. 대한민국 대통령이 취임식 다음 날 전직 일본 각료와 단 둘이 비공개 식사를 한 것은 이례적인 일입니다. 김 대통령은 마음으로부터 축하 인사를 건네는 그에게 지금부터 한일 관계를 단단히 구축해 가자고 했습니다.)

Six months later, President Kim invited Kono back to Seoul. This time, he visited South Korea on a day trip, holding a two-hour private meeting. They openly exchanged views on pending bilateral issues. Kono was later reappointed as Foreign Minister in October 1999 during DJ’s term. (고노는 “도쿄에서는 여러 차례 만났지만 서울에서 처음 만나게 된 자리가 김 대통령과의 면담이 됐다. 그가 겪어온 긴 고난의 세월을 알기에 꿈만 같은 일이었다”고 회고했습니다. 두 사람은 오랜 친구처럼 앞으로의 한일 관계를 논의했습니다.)

[Scene 2] A Letter of Consolation from DJ at 9 AM the Day After a Liver Transplant (그로부터 반년 뒤 김 대통령은 다시 고노를 서울로 초청했습니다. 이번에는 당일치기 일정으로 한국을 방문해 두 시간 동안 단둘이 회담했습니다. 양국 현안에 대한 의견을 허심탄회하게 나눴는데, 고노는 DJ 임기 중인 1999년 10월 다시 외무상으로 기용됐습니다.)

Kono underwent a liver transplant from his son, lawmaker Taro Kono, due to a worsening of his chronic hepatitis C. Politicians are usually reluctant to show their frail side. However, Kono stated that due to ongoing societal discussions in Japan about liver transplants, he made the matter public through a press conference considering its social significance. ([장면 2] 간 이식 다음 날 아 9시에 받은 DJ 위문 편지)

Then, around 9 AM the next day, an unexpected ‘guest’ arrived at the National Diet. A diplomat from the South Korean Embassy in Japan came to the parliamentarians’ office building bearing a handwritten letter of consolation from President Kim. Kono wrote, “Hearing about my surgery, President Kim must have quickly written the letter and sent it on the last flight.” This background likely explains why Kono called DJ a statesman he held in awe and reverence. (고노는 오랫동안 앓던 C형 간염 악화로 아들 고노 다로 의원으로부터 간 이식 수술을 받았습니다. 정치인은 한사코 자신의 병약한 모습을 보이기를 꺼려합니다. 하지만 고노는 일본 사회에서 간 이식에 대한 여러 논의가 있어서 사회적 의미를 고려, 기자회견을 통해 이를 공개했다고 밝혔습니다.)

A year later, as President Kim’s term neared its end, Kono decided to visit South Korea. Less than a year after his liver transplant, his doctors advised against flying. Those around him also urged him to wait until his health fully recovered, saying, “Just because he leaves the presidential office, Kim Dae-jung doesn’t disappear.” However, he insisted, “It is important to personally console President Kim, who struggled valiantly as president, at the Blue House,” and eventually boarded the plane to Seoul without informing his doctor. (그런데, 그 다음 날 아침 9시쯤 예상치 못한 ‘손님’이 국회로 찾아왔습니다. 주일 한국 대사관 소속 외교관이 김 대통령의 자필 위문 편지를 들고 의원회관을 찾아온 것입니다. 고노는 “나의 수술 소식을 듣고 아마도 김 대통령이 급히 편지를 써 마지막 항공편으로 보낸 것 같다”고 적었습니다. 고노가 DJ를 외경(畏敬)하는 정치가로 부르는 것은 이런 배경도 있을 겁니다.)

Reappointed as Foreign Minister in October 1999, one year and eight months after President Kim’s inauguration, he actively worked to improve South Korea-Japan relations. He said, “I keenly felt how important the trust between politicians transcending borders, who had supported each other since times of hardship, is. We could talk about any topic without hesitation and with ease. President Kim trusted Japan and made bold decisions on pending bilateral issues.” He particularly praised the decision to open Japan to South Korean popular culture, despite domestic opposition, as a crucial choice for developing bilateral relations. Kono recalled that in the latter half of President Kim’s term, he unfortunately felt considerable disappointment with Japanese politics. (그로부터 1년 뒤 김 대통령이 퇴임을 앞두자 고노는 한국을 방문하기로 결단을 내립니다. 간 이식 후 1년도 지나지 않아 의사들이 비행기 탑승을 만류했습니다. 주변에서도 “대통령직에서 물러난다고 해서 김대중 씨가 사라지는 것은 아니다”라며 건강이 완전히 회복된 후 방한을 권유했습니다. 하지만 그는 “대통령으로서 고군분투한 김 대통령을 청와대에서 직접 위로하는 것이 중요하다”고 주장, 결국 의사에게 알리지 않은 채 서울행 비행기에 올랐습니다.)

Kono's Criticism of Japanese Politics (김 대통령 취임 후 1년 8개월이 지난 1999년 10월 다시 외무상이 된 그는 한일 관계 개선에 적극 나섰습니다. 그는 “고난의 시절부터 서로를 지지해 온 국경을 초월한 정치인 간 신뢰가 얼마나 중요한지 절실히 느꼈다. 어떤 주제든 주저 없이, 안심하고 이야기할 수 있었다. 김 대통령은 일본을 신뢰했고 양국 현안에 대해 과감한 결단을 내려주었다”고 했습니다. 특히 국내 반대를 무릅쓰고 일본 대중문화를 개방한 결단은 한일 관계 발전을 위해 매우 중요한 선택이었다고 평가했습니다. 고노는 김 대통령 재임 후반기에는 안타깝게도 일본 정치에 대한 실망감이 적지 않았다고 회고했습니다.)

The disappointments Kono revealed in his memoir were largely twofold. The first was that even though South Korea extended its hand first, Japan did not respond sufficiently. He assessed that while President Kim opened South Korea to Japanese culture, taking on political burdens, Japan did not provide enough concrete measures of a corresponding level. (고노의 일본 정치 비판)

He wrote, “If Japan had responded in a more visible way, South Korea-Japan relations could have developed further.” Indeed, the two countries achieved the historic feat of co-hosting the 2002 FIFA World Cup. However, he expressed regret that Japan failed to move toward more bold policies and institutional mechanisms that could have expanded exchanges between the peoples of both countries in the long term and broadened mutual understanding for future generations. (고노가 회고록에서 밝힌 실망은 크게 두 가지였습니다. 첫 번째는 한국이 먼저 손을 내밀었음에도 일본이 충분히 화답하지 못했다는 점이었습니다. 김 대통령은 정치적 부담을 감수하면서까지 일본 문화를 개방했지만, 일본 측에서는 이에 상응하는 수준의 구체적 조치가 충분히 나오지 않았다고 평가했습니다.)

Kono reflected, “I, too, made various efforts as Foreign Minister, and some were realized, but I cannot say I fully met President Kim Dae-jung’s expectations.” (그는 “일본 측이 보다 눈에 보이는 방식으로 화답했다면 한일 관계는 더욱 발전할 수 있었을 것”이라고 적었습니다. 실제로 양국은 2002년 한일 월드컵 공동 개최라는 역사적인 성과를 이뤄냈습니다. 하지만 이를 넘어 양국 국민 간 교류를 장기적으로 확대하고 미래 세대의 상호 이해를 넓힐 수 있는 보다 과감한 정책과 제도적 장치까지는 일본이 나아가지 못했다고 아쉬움을 나타냈습니다.)

The second disappointment Kono identified was the issue of Prime Minister Junichiro Koizumi’s visits to Yasukuni Shrine. After taking office in April 2001, Koizumi visited Yasukuni Shrine in August of the same year and again in April 2002. Both visits occurred during President Kim’s term. (고노는 “나 역시 외무대신으로서 여러 노력을 기울였고 일부는 실현됐지만, 김대중 대통령의 기대에 충분히 부응했다고 말할 수는 없다”고 회고했습니다.)

Kono assessed that Koizumi’s Yasukuni visits severely damaged not only South Korea-Japan relations but also relations with China. He viewed it as a symbolic event that shook the hard-won trust between South Korea and Japan. (고노가 꼽은 두 번째 실망은 고이즈미 준이치로 총리의 야스쿠니 신사 참배 문제였습니다. 고이즈미는 2001년 4월 취임 후, 같은 해 8월 야스쿠니 신사를 참배했고, 이듬해인 2002년 4월에도 다시 참배했습니다. 두 차례 모두 김 대통령 재임 기간 중에 이뤄진 일이었습니다.)

At the time, he sought his own alternatives to resolve the issue. Before visiting South Korea, he conveyed to then-Chief Cabinet Secretary Yasuo Fukuda (later Prime Minister) his opinion that “a plan should be considered to create a new national memorial facility where anyone can pay respects without hesitation.” He believed that a new commemorative space, free from specific religious colors or historical controversy, was necessary to resolve the domestic and international conflicts surrounding Yasukuni Shrine visits. He also reportedly asked directly how far discussions within a government advisory body on this matter had progressed. Chief Cabinet Secretary Fukuda replied, “I cannot promise when actual construction will be possible, but the process is moving forward.” (고노는 그의 야스쿠니 참배가 한일 관계뿐 아니라 중국과의 관계에도 심각한 악영향을 미쳤다고 평가했습니다. 어렵게 구축해 온 한일 간 신뢰를 흔드는 상징적 사건이었다고 봤습니다.)

Kono also conveyed this information to President Kim. It is said that President Kim, upon hearing that the Japanese government was working to resolve the issue, expressed some understanding. However, the plan to build a new memorial facility ultimately did not materialize. In his memoir, Kono mentioned this issue, lamenting that the flow of South Korea-Japan reconciliation and trust, built with such difficulty, was not sufficiently sustained due to the limitations of Japanese politics. (그는 당시 문제 해결을 위해 나름의 대안을 모색하기도 했습니다. 방한에 앞서 후쿠다 야스오 당시 관방장관(나중에 총리)에게 “누구나 거리낌 없이 추도할 수 있는 새로운 국립 추모시설을 만드는 방안을 검토해야 한다”는 의견을 전달했습니다. 야스쿠니 신사 참배를 둘러싼 국내외 갈등을 해소하기 위해서는 특정 종교색이나 역사 논란에서 벗어난 새로운 추모 공간이 필요하다고 판단했던 겁다. 아울러 이 문제와 관련한 정부 자문기구의 논의가 어디까지 진행됐는지도 직접 물었다고 합니다. 이에 대해 후쿠다 장관은 “언제 실제 건설이 가능할지는 약속할 수 없지만 절차는 진행되고 있다”고 답했습니다.)

He was, to that extent, a politician who tried to keep promises based on trust with DJ. We remember the life and achievements of Yohei Kono, a Japanese politician who was a pillar of future-oriented South Korea-Japan relations, and express our deepest condolences. (고노는 이 같은 내용을 김 대통령에게도 전달했습니다. 당시 김 대통령은 일본 정부가 문제 해결을 위해 노력하고 있다는 설명을 듣고 어느 정도 이해를 보였다고 합니다. 그러나 결과적으로 새로운 추모 시설 건립 구상은 실현되지 못했습니다. 고노는 회고록에서 이 문제를 언급하며, 당시 어렵게 쌓아 올린 한일 화해와 신뢰의 흐름이 일본 정치의 한계로 인해 충분히 이어지지 못한 점을 안타까워했습니다.)

(그만큼 그는 DJ와의 신뢰에 기반한 약속을 지키려 한 정치인이었습니다. 미래지향적 한일관계의 버팀목이었던 일본 정치인 고노 요헤이의 삶과 업적을 기억하며 깊은 애도의 뜻을 표합니다.)

item.title: North Korea Rebukes US-South Korea NCG Meeting’s Mention of ‘Denuclearization’ as “Empty Delusion” (北, 한미 NCG 회의 ‘비핵화’ 언급에 반발 “공허한 망상”)
item.description:
North Korea Rebukes US-South Korea NCG Meeting’s Mention of ‘Denuclearization’ as “Empty Delusion” (北, 한미 NCG 회의 ‘비핵화’ 언급에 반발 “공허한 망상”)

In response to the US and South Korea reaffirming the goal of “North Korea’s denuclearization” at the Nuclear Consultative Group (NCG), a body for extended deterrence, North Korea stated that “talking about disarming a belligerent counterpart is nothing but a preposterous and empty delusion.” (북한은 한미가 확장억제 협의체인 핵협의그룹(NCG) 회의에서 ‘북한 비핵화’ 목표를 확인한 것과 관련해 “교전 상대방의 핵무장 해제를 운운하는 것이야말로 어불성설이며 공허한 망상”이라고 했다.)

A spokesperson for North Korea’s Foreign Ministry, in a statement released through the Korean Central News Agency on the 14th, said, “We sternly denounce and reject the collective nuclear confrontation racket of the US, Japan, and South Korea, as well as the impure attempts by Western countries to impose unconstitutional acts on sovereign nations on the international stage,” and “We issue a warning about the consequences that the repetition of such provocative acts may bring.” (북한 외무성 대변인은 14일 조선중앙통신을 통해 발표한 담화에서 “집단적 성격을 띤 미일한의 핵 대결 소동과 국제 무대에서 주권 국가에 위헌 행위를 강요하려는 서방 나라들의 불순한 기도를 엄정히 규탄·배격”한다며 “도발 행위의 반복성이 초래할 후과에 대해 경종을 울린다”고 했다.)

The spokesperson added, “The meaningless anti-DPRK rhetoric and nuclear threat collaboration of the US and its followers can have no impact whatsoever on our irreversible status as a nuclear weapons state,” and “Denuclearization is a matter that has been finally and irreversibly concluded.” (대변인은 “미국과 추종 세력들의 무의미한 반공화국 비난 수사와 핵 위협 공조는 되돌릴 수 없는 우리의 핵보유국 지위에 아무러한 영향도 미칠 수 없다”며 “‘비핵화’는 최종적으로 되돌릴 수 없이 종결된 사안”이라고 했다.)

Referring to US-Japan-South Korea arms deals and joint exercises predicated on nuclear use, the spokesperson said, “This fully demonstrates the reasons and justification for us to more thoroughly commit to strengthening necessary self-defense capabilities to ensure national security.” (대변인은 한미일 무기 거래와 핵 사용을 전제로 한 연합 연습 등을 언급하며 “우리가 국가의 안전을 보장하기 위한 필수적인 자위력 강화에 보다 전념해야 할 이유와 당위성을 충분히 입증한다”고 했다.)

He further stated, “Building a nuclear shield is a lawful process aimed at deterring external interference and threats, ensuring national sovereignty and security, and guaranteeing regional peace and stability.” (이어 “핵 방패 구축은 외부로부터의 간섭과 위협을 억제하고 국가의 주권과 안전을 담보하며 지역의 평화와 안정을 보장하기 위한 합법칙적 과정”이라고 했다.)

He stressed, “No matter how much the US, Japan, and South Korea argue, they will never change the current status of the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea as a nuclear weapons state,” and “No one can salvage the concept of ‘denuclearization,’ which has permanently disappeared in the flow of the times.” (그러면서 “미·일·한 3국이 아무리 강변해도 핵보유국으로서의 조선민주주의인민공화국의 현 지위를 절대로 변경시키지 못할 것”이라며 “그 누구도 시대적 흐름 속에 영구적으로 실종된 ‘비핵화’를 건져낼 수 없을 것”이라고 했다.)

Earlier, on the 11th, the US and South Korea held the 6th NCG meeting in Seoul and issued a joint press statement specifying that “both sides confirmed the shared goal of North Korea’s denuclearization.” (앞서 한미는 지난 11일 서울에서 제6차 NCG 회의를 열고 “북한의 비핵화에 대한 공동의 목표를 확인했다”는 내용을 명시한 공동 언론 성명을 발표했다.)

The previous day, North Korea also criticized the Donald Trump administration’s approval of arms sales, including medium-range air-to-air missiles to South Korea, calling it a “provocative arms buildup maneuver.” (북한은 전날도 도널드 트럼프 미국 행정부가 한국에 중거리 공대공 미사일 등 무기 판매를 승인한 데 대해 “도발적인 무력 증강 책동”이라고 했다.)

item.title: Ahn Gyu-back: "OPCON Transition Target Year to be Coordinated with U.S., Proposed to Both Presidents by Year-End" (안규백 “전작권 전환 목표연도, 美와 조율... 연말 양국 대통령에 건의”)
item.description:
Ahn Gyu-back: "OPCON Transition Target Year to be Coordinated with U.S., Proposed to Both Presidents by Year-End" (안규백 “전작권 전환 목표연도, 美와 조율... 연말 양국 대통령에 건의”)

Defense Minister Ahn Gyu-back stated on the 14th that he would propose a target year for the transition of wartime operational control (OPCON) from South Korea to the U.S. to the presidents of both countries by the end of this year. (안규백 국방부 장관은 14일 한국의 전시작전통제권(전작권) 전환 목표 연도를 올해 연말 양국 대통령에게 건의하겠다고 밝혔다.)

Appearing on KBS’s "Sunday Diagnosis" program that day, Minister Ahn said, "We will discuss the validation of Full Operational Capability (FOC) in November with the U.S. Secretary of Defense at the Security Consultative Meeting (SCM), and based on that, we will make a proposal to the presidents of both countries. Then, we will determine the X-year (target year) for the restoration of OPCON." (안 장관은 이날 KBS 일요진단에 출연해 “완전운용능력(FOC) 검증을 올해 11월 미 국방장관과 한미안보협의회(SCM)에서 논의하고 이걸 기초로 양국 대통령에게 건의할 것”이라며 “그러면 전작권 회복의 X연도(목표 연도)를 결정하게 된다”고 말했다.)

As the Lee Jae-myung administration views the timing of the OPCON transition as "possibly as early as next year," there are also observations that 2027 could be proposed as the target year for OPCON transition. The U.S. Forces Korea sees the achievement of transition conditions as "possibly as early as the first quarter of 2029." (이재명 정부는 전작권 전환 시점을 ‘이르면 내년’으로 보는 만큼 2027년이 전작권 전환의 목표 연도로 제시될 수 있다는 관측도 나온다. 주한 미군은 전환 조건의 달성 시점을 ‘이르면 2029년 1분기’로 보고 있다.)

When asked if there are differing views between South Korea and the U.S. on the timing of the OPCON transition, Minister Ahn responded, "Differences in opinion are possible. Even between spouses, thoughts can differ, so how can it be that the views of two countries on the OPCON issue are identical?" (안 장관은 한미 간 전작권 전환 시기에 대한 견해차가 있느냐는 질문에 “다른 견해가 있을 수 있다”며 “부부간에도 생각이 다른데, 나라와 나라 사이에서 전작권 문제에 대해 의견이 동일할 수 있겠나”라고 했다.)

He added, "At this point, our capabilities are needed to narrow those differences," and said that they are communicating closely with the U.S. to achieve this. (그러면서 “그 이견을 좁히는 것에 우리의 역량이 필요한 시점”이라며 이를 위해 미국과 긴밀하게 소통하고 있다고도 했다.)

Regarding a question about whether the conditions for OPCON transition previously agreed upon by South Korea and the U.S. can reflect changes in modern warfare, such as the use of drones, Minister Ahn stated, "New weapons emerge every day, and the battlefield landscape changes day by day. If that's the case, wouldn't the conditions be like waiting for the Yellow River to clear (a Korean idiom meaning something that may never happen)?" He added, "While the battlefield paradigm has changed significantly, our capabilities are sufficient." (안 장관은 과거 한미가 합의한 전작권 전환의 조건이 무인기 등 달라진 현대전 양상을 반영할 수 있느냐는 질문에는 “매일 새로운 무기가 나오고 하루가 다르게 전장 양상이 달라지는데, 그럼 조건이라는 게 백년하청(百年河淸) 아니냐”며 “전장 패러다임이 많이 바뀌었지만, 우리의 능력은 충분하다”고 했다.)

He further said, "South Korea and the U.S. have promised a 'conditions-based OPCON transition,' and we have faithfully evaluated capabilities according to those conditions. In my view, after recovering OPCON, we should discuss those matters." (그러면서 “한미가 ‘조건에 의한 전작권 회복’을 약속했고, 그에 따라 조건에 대한 능력 평가를 성실히 해왔다”며 “전작권을 회복한 뒤 그런 사항을 논의해야 한다는 것이 제 생각”이라고 했다.)

Regarding the "Jangbogo N Project," which aims to deploy a Korean-style nuclear-powered submarine (NPS) in the 2030s, Minister Ahn said, "South Korea has all the necessary conditions, including submarine and nuclear technology. We only lack nuclear fuel, and we plan to seek cooperation and support from the U.S. for low-enriched uranium of less than 20%." (안 장관은 2030년대 한국형 원자력 추진 잠수함(원잠)을 전력화한다는 ‘장보고 N사업’에 대해선 “한국은 잠수함과 원자력 기술 등 모든 조건을 갖추고 있다”며 “단지 핵연료만 없는데, 20％ 미만의 저농축 우라늄을 미국 측에 협조받고 지원받을 생각”이라고 했다.)

When asked if the domestic construction of the NPS had been agreed upon with the U.S., he responded, "It hasn't reached an agreement yet," but added, "It has been our consistent stance that it should be built domestically with our technology, and the U.S. side is in the process of understanding that." (원잠 국내 건조를 미국과 합의했느냐는 질문에는 “아직 합의까진 아니다”라면서도 “국내에서 우리 기술로 만들어야 한다는 것이 우리의 일관된 입장이고, 미측도 그렇게 이해하고 있는 과정”이라고 했다.)

item.title: Ruling and Opposition Clash Over Judiciary Committee Chair... People Power Party: "Opposition Must Defend It" Democratic Party: "Blatant Hypocrisy, Cannot Give It Away" (與野, 법사위원장 놓고 격돌…국힘 “야당이 사수해야” 민주 “적반하장, 못 넘겨”)
item.description:
Ruling and Opposition Clash Over Judiciary Committee Chair... People Power Party: "Opposition Must Defend It" Democratic Party: "Blatant Hypocrisy, Cannot Give It Away" (與野, 법사위원장 놓고 격돌…국힘 “야당이 사수해야” 민주 “적반하장, 못 넘겨”)

The ruling and opposition parties are engaging in a tense standoff over who will hold the chairmanship of the Legislation and Judiciary Committee, ahead of negotiations for the formation of the second half of the 22nd National Assembly. The People Power Party (PPP) argued that "the opposition party defending the Judiciary Committee chairmanship reflects the public sentiment from the June 3 local elections," while the Democratic Party (DP) countered that "the PPP's demand for the Judiciary Committee chairmanship is a blatantly hypocritical claim." (여야가 22대 국회 후반기 원 구성 협상을 앞두고 법제사법위원장 자리를 서로 갖겠다며 신경전을 벌이고 있다. 국민의힘은 “야당이 법사위원장을 사수하는 게 6·3 지방선거의 민심”이라고 한 반면, 더불어민주당은 “국민의힘의 법사위원장 자리 요구는 적반하장식 주장”이라며 맞섰다.)

Choi Bo-yoon, senior spokesperson for the PPP, stated in a commentary on the 14th that "defending the Judiciary Committee chairmanship and fully restoring the National Assembly's oversight function is the only way to heed the stern public sentiment from the June 3 local elections, which called for preventing the privatization of power." Senior Spokesperson Choi added, "The last bastion to check and neutralize the DP's unilateral flood of special counsel bills and the Ministry of Justice's cunning abuse of authority is solely the Judiciary Committee. To thwart the administration's efforts to destroy the judiciary, the opposition party must take on the Judiciary Committee chairmanship." (최보윤 국민의힘 수석대변인은 14일 논평에서 “법사위원장직을 사수해 국회의 견제 기능을 온전히 복원하는 것만이 권력의 사유화를 막으라는 6·3 지방선거의 준엄한 민심을 따르는 길”이라고 했다. 최 수석대변인은 “민주당의 일방적인 특검법 폭주와 법무부의 꼼수 권한 남용을 견제하고 무력화할 수 있는 마지막 보루는 오직 법사위뿐”이라면서 “정권의 사법 파괴 책동을 막아내기 위해 야당이 법사위원장직을 반드시 맡아야 한다”고 했다.)

Choi Soo-jin, senior deputy spokesperson for the floor, also criticized the DP in a commentary on the same day, stating that "declaring a monopoly on the Judiciary Committee chairmanship is a declaration of continued parliamentary dictatorship." Senior Deputy Spokesperson Choi said, "The DP, following the National Assembly Speaker, is now seeking to monopolize even the Judiciary Committee chairmanship, blatantly revealing its intention to reject dialogue and compromise politics and continue unilateral legislation. The DP's rampage, which disregards parliamentarism, must be stopped immediately." (최수진 원내수석대변인도 같은 날 논평에서 민주당을 향해 “법사위원장 독식 선언은 의회 독재를 지속하겠다는 선전포고”라고 했다. 최 원내수석대변인은 “민주당은 국회의장에 이어 법사위원장까지 독식하겠다고 나서며, 대화와 타협의 정치를 거부하고 일방통행식 입법을 지속하겠다는 의도를 노골적으로 드러내고 있다”면서 “의회주의를 무시한 민주당의 폭주는 즉각 중단돼야 한다”고 했다.)

In contrast, Lee Joo-hee, deputy floor spokesperson for the DP, said in a written briefing on the 13th that "the PPP's demand for the National Assembly's Legislation and Judiciary Committee chairmanship, given its history of delaying legislation, is merely a forced argument that fails to reflect on the past." Deputy Floor Spokesperson Lee added, "The PPP's demand for the Judiciary Committee chairmanship, invoking the principle of checks and balances, is a hypocritical claim that forgets its irresponsible track record of obstructing the National Assembly. The public remembers the PPP's old habits of tying up even bipartisan livelihood bills with comprehensive filibusters, grinding the National Assembly to a halt." (반면 이주희 민주당 원내대변인은 13일 서면 브리핑에서 “입법 지연을 일삼아온 국민의힘의 국회 법제사법위원장 요구는 과거를 성찰하지 않은 억지일 뿐”이라고 했다. 이 원내대변인은 “국민의힘이 견제와 균형의 원리를 언급하며 법사위원장 자리를 요구하는 건 그간 저지른 무책임한 국회 발목잡기 행적을 망각한 적반하장식 주장”이라면서 “여야가 합의한 민생 법안까지 싸잡아 전방위 필리버스터로 묶어 국회를 공전시킨 국민의힘의 구태를 국민은 기억한다”고 했다.)

Deputy Floor Spokesperson Lee stated, "We can never give the position of Judiciary Committee chair, which can halt all standing committee bills and tie the National Assembly's hands, to the PPP, which has consistently delayed legislation. It is essential for the ruling party to hold the Judiciary Committee chairmanship to quickly support the government's policy agenda through legislation and to push forward the pending livelihood bills without unnecessary delays." (이 원내대변인은 “모든 상임위 법안을 계류시켜 국회의 발을 묶을 수 있는 법사위원장 자리를 입법 지연을 일삼아온 국민의힘에 결코 넘겨줄 수 없다”면서 “집권당이 법사위원장을 하는 건 정부 국정 과제를 신속하게 입법으로 뒷받침하고 지금도 계류 중인 민생 입법을 최대한 공회전 없이 추진하기 위해 필수적”이라고 했다.)

The Judiciary Committee is a key standing committee that serves as a gateway for passing bills in the National Assembly. Since the 16th National Assembly, there was a tradition where the largest party held the speakership and the second-largest party held the Judiciary Committee chairmanship. However, this practice was disrupted in the first half of the 20th National Assembly when the ruling Saenuri Party took the Judiciary Committee chairmanship. In the first half of the 21st National Assembly, the DP held all 18 standing committee chairs, and since then, the ruling and opposition parties have fiercely contested the Judiciary Committee chairmanship in each round of organizational negotiations. (법사위는 국회 법안 통과의 관문 역할을 하는 핵심 상임위다. 16대 국회부터는 제1당이 국회의장, 제2당이 법사위원장을 맡는 관행이 이어졌지만, 2016년 20대 국회 전반기에서 여당인 새누리당이 법사위원장을 가져가며 관행이 흔들렸다. 21대 국회 전반기 때는 민주당이 18개 상임위원장을 모두 맡았고, 이후 원 구성 협상 때마다 여야가 법사위원장 자리를 놓고 치열하게 다투고 있다.)

item.title: Cho Seung-rae: "President Lee Emphasizes Ruling Party's Responsibility... Interpretation Targeting Leadership Is Distortion" (조승래 “李대통령, 與책임 강조... ‘지도부 겨냥’ 해석은 왜곡”)
item.description:
Cho Seung-rae: "President Lee Emphasizes Ruling Party's Responsibility... Interpretation Targeting Leadership Is Distortion" (조승래 “李대통령, 與책임 강조... ‘지도부 겨냥’ 해석은 왜곡”)

Cho Seung-rae, Secretary-General of the Democratic Party of Korea, stated on the 14th regarding some interpretations that President Lee Jae-myung's message emphasizing the ruling party's responsibility was targeting the leadership of Jeong Cheong-rae: "That is a distortion of the President's intent." (조승래 더불어민주당 사무총장은 14일 여당의 책임을 강조한 이재명 대통령의 메시지가 정청래 지도부를 겨냥한 것이란 일각의 해석에 대해 “대통령의 뜻을 왜곡하는 것”이라고 했다.)

Secretary-General Cho made this remark during a press briefing held at the National Assembly, saying, "I understand that the message was not directed at a specific individual or leadership, but rather to emphasize the responsibility of how the ruling party should operate state affairs after the local elections." (조 사무총장은 이날 국회에서 열린 기자간담회에서 “그 메시지는 특정 개인이나 지도부라기보다는 여당이 지방선거 이후 어떤 자세로 국정 운영을 해야 될 것인지 책임성을 강조하기 위한 걸로 이해하고 있다”면서 이같이 밝혔다.)

The previous day, President Lee posted a lengthy message on X (formerly Twitter) stating that "The passion of the ruling party should be directed not at 'our camp,' but at the entire people." In the post, President Lee emphasized the ruling party's responsibility, using expressions such as "For the ruling party, the ability and performance to take responsibility with given power, as well as inclusivity and integration, are important" and "The ruling party in power must focus on the 'language of responsibility.'" Some in the ruling party interpreted that this post was aimed at Representative Jeong Cheong-rae, who, ahead of his bid for reelection as party leader, has been issuing messages targeting hardline party members, such as the "abolition of the supplementary investigation power." (이 대통령은 전날 X(옛 트위터)에 “여당의 열정은 ‘우리 진영’이 아니라 국민 전체를 향해야 한다”는 취지의 장문의 글을 올렸다. 이 대통령은 글에서 “여당은 주어진 권력으로 책임을 지는 능력과 실적, 포용과 통합이 중요하다” “집권 여당은 ‘책임의 언어’에 집중해야 한다” 등의 표현으로 여당의 책임론을 강조했다. 여권 일각에선 이 글이 당대표 연임 도전을 앞두고 ‘보완 수사권 폐지’ 등 강성 당원들을 겨냥한 메시지를 쏟아내고 있는 정청래 대표를 겨냥한 것이란 해석이 나왔다.)

Secretary-General Cho stated that the post "was not aimed at a specific individual or leadership" and added, "If the President's intent is misinterpreted, that itself narrows the President's broader vision." (조 사무총장은 해당 글이 “특정 개인이나 지도부를 겨냥한 것은 아니다”라면서 “대통령 뜻을 곡해한다면 그 자체가 대통령의 큰 뜻을 오히려 좁히는 것”이라고 했다.)

Secretary-General Cho also repeatedly emphasized the achievements of the June 3 local elections. Cho stated, "2,294 out of 3,192 candidates were elected," adding, "An election rate of 72% is unprecedented. I believe such achievements should also be evaluated together." He continued, "People often say, 'We lost because we lost Seoul,' or 'Honam was too chaotic.' Those points are valid. But in the end, we achieved an unprecedented victory in the basic local government head positions." He noted, "Out of 41 basic local government head seats in Honam, we won 29 in 2018, but this year, we won all except 5 in South Jeolla (winning 36)," and "In Seoul, out of 25 district mayors, we lost 18 to 7 in 2022, but this time, the results were reversed." (조 사무총장은 6·3 지방선거 성과도 거듭 강조했다. 조 사무총장은 “3192명이 출마해서 2294명이 당선됐다”면서 “72%의 당선률은 역대급이다. 이런 것도 같이 평가해야 한다고 생각한다”고 했다. 이어 “흔히 ‘서울 졌으니까 졌다’, ‘호남 너무 어수선했다’ (하는데) 맞는 얘기다. 그런데 결과적으로는 기초단체장은 역대급 승리를 했다”고 했다. 그는 “호남 기초단체장 41곳 중 2018년에는 29곳에서 당선됐는데, 올해는 전남 5곳 빼고 (36곳에서) 다 이겼다”면서 “서울에서도 25개 구청장 중 2022년 18 대 7로 졌는데 이번엔 거꾸로 됐다”고 했다.)

Secretary-General Cho also said that the impact of articles reported before and after early voting, which discussed the next party leadership election for the Democratic Party, should be assessed. He stated, "The internal fractures in Pyeongtaek and North Jeolla were linked to the next party leadership structure, revealing those fractures to the public," adding, "We must make a cold-headed evaluation of that." He further said, "If the articles conveyed facts incorrectly, there may also be issues with the media," and asked, "For example, during the local elections, reports that the Prime Minister would step down to run for party leadership—how would that influence the election? The involved parties did not deny the articles, but was that really appropriate?" This was interpreted as a remark targeting Prime Minister Kim Min-seok, who is likely to run for the next party leadership. (조 사무총장은 사전투표 전후 보도됐던 민주당 차기 당권설 관련 기사가 선거에 어떤 영향을 미쳤는지도 평가해야 한다고 했다. 그는 “평택과 전북에서 있었던 당내 균열적 구조를 차기 당권 구도와 연결지으면서 있었던 균열을 국민들께 보여줬다”면서 “그것에 대해선 냉정한 평가를 해야 한다”고 했다. 또 “기사가 팩트와 다르게 전달됐다면 언론사에도 문제가 있을 것”이라면서 “예를 들면 지선 진행 중인데 총리 그만두고 당권 도전한다, 이런 게 선거에 어떤 영향을 줬겠느냐. 기사에 대해 당사자들이 부인하지 않았는데 그게 과연 적절했느냐”고 했다. 이는 차기 당대표 출마가 유력한 김민석 국무총리를 겨냥한 말로 해석됐다.)
